fields.why: The Summary's headline contrasts are stated multiples ('three times more likely', 'approximately twice as high'), which are relative, and Table 2 reports dollar differences, which are absolute. 'absolute' alone misses the relative headline claims.

Each per-age ecologic linear model has one row per parish (19 parishes) and no repeated or nested units, so 'none' (the model plainly has nothing to account for) is defensible. The article says nothing about it, so the silent default null is also defensible.

brief_issues: Only record B was provided, so A's justification was not rated. The brief does not say whether a one-row-per-unit ecologic regression counts as 'plainly has none to account for' (giving 'none') or as silent (giving null).
